Synapse 1.165.0, Element X signs itself back in, and security updates reach the published image every week.

## ✨ Added

- **A compose file for other Docker hosts.** `compose.yaml` runs Matrix on any Linux server with Docker, and the README covers Synology, Proxmox and MOS.

## 🎨 Design

- The README groups its download buttons under titles, with a MOS button next to the compose file and the source, and draws the section headings as chapter bands.

## ⚡ Improved

- **Synapse [v1.165.0](https://github.com/element-hq/synapse/releases/tag/v1.165.0), Element Web [v1.12.35](https://github.com/element-hq/element-web/releases/tag/v1.12.35), Ketesa [v1.5.2](https://github.com/etkecc/ketesa/releases/tag/v1.5.2) and Matrix Authentication Service [1.29.0](https://github.com/element-hq/matrix-authentication-service/releases/tag/v1.29.0).**
- **Fixed Python packages in place of the ones Synapse ships.** authlib 1.9.10, joserfc 1.8.0, pyasn1 0.6.5, soupsieve 4.1.3, tornado 6.6.1, Twisted 26.10.0, setuptools 84.2.1 and pip 26.3 close the open advisories, one of them critical.
- **gosu is built from source with Go 1.27.4** and a current x/sys, and sits at `/usr/sbin/gosu` where Synapse's start script looks for it. The builds in Synapse's image and upstream use Go 1.24, which has open advisories.
- s6-overlay, which starts and supervises the services in the container, is at 3.2.3.2.
- **Debian security updates go in with every build** and never come from the build cache, so fixes published after Synapse built its image are included.
- **The published image stays current between releases.** Every Sunday the newest release is rebuilt without the cache, and every Monday pending Debian updates go on top of `latest`. When nothing changed, nothing is pushed.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Element X refreshes its sign-in by itself again.** Synapse 1.164 dropped the address Element X uses to refresh its token, so it could claim it cannot reach the homeserver. Synapse 1.164.2 answers it again, and the proxy rule from the [setup guide](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/matrix/blob/main/docs/setup.md#element-x-says-it-cant-reach-the-homeserver) is no longer needed.
- **Scanners see the libpq5 that is really installed.** Synapse's image kept a record of the older 17.11, and scanners reported 47 advisories against it. The image drops such records once apt has upgraded the library.
